philosophy: The roster is valuable because Titans solve different tactical problems, not because missions require specific ownership.

Defender.tacticalProblems: long survival, objective holding, hazard endurance

Battery.tacticalProblems: resource pressure, Divinity/Momentum economy, long missions

Controller.tacticalProblems: fast enemies, terrain-heavy battles, caster denial

Breaker.tacticalProblems: heavily armored enemies, shield windows, boss armor phases

Disruptor.tacticalProblems: enemy casters, elite mechanics, Momentum/Divinity denial

Artillery.tacticalProblems: large enemy groups, ranged pressure, objective zones

Guardian.tacticalProblems: boss duels, counterattack, protection under pressure

Assassin.tacticalProblems: execution-based encounters, priority targets, mobility assassinations

overlapFindings.finding: No raw role-count redundancy; each faction has all nine current role identities. Risk remains if roles only change numbers, so solo mechanics must stay unique.

titansNeedingDesignAttention.criterion: Any Titan whose live implementation still has generic basic/skill/ultimate only
titansNeedingDesignAttention.action: Convert to unique resource, reaction, stance, execution, gear, and Divine Ascension mechanics before content lock.

favoredNotRequiredRule: Missions may show advantages and recommended Titans/builds, but never ownership locks.
